No immediate complications were observed.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Giant cell bone tumour, Campanacci stage III
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old woman presented with pain, tenderness, and swelling in her left middle finger. Initial X-ray showed a geographic osteolytic lesion, and MRI suggested an enchondroma. After 6 months, with no improvement in symptoms, repeat imaging showed progression of an expansile osteolytic lesion with articular involvement, indicating an aggressive tumor. Histopathology confirmed giant cell bone tumour, classified as Campanacci stage III. The patient underwent middle phalanx resection and interphalangeal joint arthrodesis with iliac bone graft. At 1-year follow-up, she was pain-free with functional attenuation due to phalangeal fusion and no sign of recurrence.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with pain, tenderness, and swelling in the left middle finger, with a swollen and tender mass at the middle phalanx.
Initial plain radiography showed a geographic osteolytic lesion on the shaft of the middle phalanx with a well-defined sclerotic border, no periosteal reaction or fracture line.
MRI showed a hypointense solid intramedullary lesion with hyperintense surrounding soft tissue, initially considered an enchondroma with pathological fracture.
At 6-month follow-up, symptoms persisted, and repeat plain radiograph showed progression of an expansile osteolytic lesion with articular involvement, indicating an aggressive tumor.
Histopathology confirmed giant cell bone tumour, classified as Campanacci stage III.
Treatment involved middle phalanx resection and interphalangeal joint arthrodesis with iliac bone graft.
At 1-year follow-up, the patient was pain-free with functional attenuation and no sign of GCT recurrence.
